proof_summary: The \(\pm1\) condition implies every unit has \((m-1)\)-st power \(1\), so the Carmichael exponent divides \(m-1\); if \(p^2\mid m\), the factor \(p\) in \(\lambda(p^2)=p(p-1)\) would then divide both \(m\) and \(m-1\), proving that \(m\) is squarefree. Thus a composite odd \(m\) factors as coprime \(d e\) with \(d,e\ge3\), and any hypothetical \(b^n=-1\) yields via CRT the unit \(x=(b,1)\), whose \(n\)-th power is \((-1,1)\), neither \(1\) nor \(-1\), contradicting the defining condition.
